edits.title: Normalize Pyserini casing
edits.find: [PySerini API](https://github.com/castorini/pyserini)
edits.replacement: [Pyserini API](https://github.com/castorini/pyserini)
edits.comment: Use the same Pyserini capitalization used later in the post.

edits.title: Smooth scale sentence
edits.find: I've embedded datasets before, just nothing on this scale; making it work across 553 million documents poses additional challenges:
edits.replacement: I've embedded datasets before, but nothing on this scale. Making it work across 553 million documents poses additional challenges:
edits.comment: Avoids the informal comma splice before 'just' and makes the transition clearer.

edits.title: Fix ClimbMix casing in diagram
edits.find: Fetch the original Climbmix document
edits.replacement: Fetch the original ClimbMix document
edits.comment: Use the dataset capitalization established in the introduction.

edits.title: Fix ClimbMix row casing
edits.find: ClimbmixCorpus row
edits.replacement: ClimbMixCorpus row
edits.comment: Keeps the generated entity name consistent with ClimbMix.

edits.title: Split API route sentence
edits.find:
The first route is primarily what we need, the others allow us to interface with 
PySerini more easily by allowing us to pull original documents or metadata that can be used 
to implement RRF/other methods.
edits.replacement: The first route is primarily what we need. The others let us interface with Pyserini more easily by pulling original documents or metadata that can be used to implement RRF and other methods.
edits.comment: The original is a comma splice and repeats 'allowing us'.

edits.title: Fix API hosting spacing
edits.section: How the API (and other tooling) is Hosted
edits.find:
Beyond hosting the API there are other needs. Concretely we need to embed queries at run time,
bulk embed queries when creating the index, store the dense embedding index, and  store the metadata
edits.replacement: Beyond hosting the API, there are other needs. Concretely, we need to embed queries at runtime, bulk embed queries when creating the index, store the dense embedding index, and store the metadata
edits.comment: Adds missing commas, removes a double space, and uses 'runtime' consistently as a noun.

edits.title: Use Kubernetes name
edits.section: How the API (and other tooling) is Hosted
edits.find: A K8 cluster of 16 L4s that runs when indexing the dataset
edits.replacement: A Kubernetes cluster of 16 L4s that runs when indexing the dataset
edits.comment: 'K8' is less standard than Kubernetes or K8s.

edits.title: Fix SQL intro wording
edits.find: Ok now that we have the corpus in a SQL db, we can iterate over the table.
edits.replacement: Now that we have the corpus in a SQL database, we can iterate over the table.
edits.comment: Removes an informal opener and avoids inconsistent 'db' casing.

edits.title: Fix producer-consumer lead-in
edits.find:
To do this with enough speed a multi-producer, multi-consumer architecture was used.
 Documents are fed into a queue by each producer,
edits.replacement: To do this with enough speed, a multi-producer, multi-consumer architecture was used. Documents are fed into a queue by each producer,
edits.comment: Adds the missing comma and removes the extra leading space before 'Documents'.

edits.title: Fix FAISS index sentence
edits.find:
The indices themselves are using inner product, built with normalized vectors, using IVFPQ, and 
use explicit IDs to map entries back to the PostgreSQL database.
edits.replacement: The indices use inner product with normalized vectors, use IVFPQ, and store explicit IDs to map entries back to the PostgreSQL database.
edits.comment: Fixes the parallel structure and removes repeated 'using'.

edits.title: Reduce merge slang
edits.find: Just be mindful that the merge takes a hot minute and is proportional to the amount of data and number of files present. With the full run it takes about 2-3 days on a 16 core machine, using ~20 GB
edits.replacement: Just be mindful that the merge takes a long time and is proportional to the amount of data and number of files present. With the full run, it takes about 2-3 days on a 16-core machine, using ~20 GB
edits.comment: Replaces slang and hyphenates the compound modifier.

edits.title: Hyphenate scale modifiers
edits.find:
While small scale testing highlighted 
most issues, there are a couple I only discovered after the first full scale run.
edits.replacement: While small-scale testing highlighted most issues, there are a couple I only discovered after the first full-scale run.
edits.comment: Hyphenate compound modifiers and remove the unnecessary line break.

edits.title: Remove informal aside
edits.find:
can accurately represent (there is an information-theoretical limit for lossless representation, but getting an accurate estimate is hard so just trust me bro)
we chunk data.
edits.replacement: can accurately represent (there is an information-theoretical limit for lossless representation, but getting an accurate estimate is hard), we chunk data.
edits.comment: 'Just trust me bro' is funny but too informal for this explanatory section.

edits.title: Use bottleneck consistently
edits.find: so it doesn't become a choke point.
edits.replacement: so it doesn't become a bottleneck.
edits.comment: The post alternates between choke point, chokepoint, and bottleneck; 'bottleneck' is clearer.

edits.title: Fix tokenizer comparison
edits.find: comparatively slow to other options
edits.replacement: comparatively slow compared with other options
edits.comment: Use 'compared with' rather than 'slow to'.

edits.title: Replace yeeting slang
edits.find: compared to just yeeting whole documents
edits.replacement: compared to embedding whole documents directly
edits.comment: Replaces slang with clearer technical wording.

edits.title: Use code formatting for formula
edits.find: I set the limit to $$3.5 * max\_num\_tokens$$ characters.
edits.replacement: I set the limit to `3.5 * max_num_tokens` characters.
edits.comment: This is an inline expression rather than display math; code formatting avoids LaTeX escaping issues.

edits.title: Fix trade-off comma splice
edits.find:
In hindsight I would pick a value of 2.5, that seems like the best compromise
between size and unembedded text.
edits.replacement: In hindsight, I would pick a value of 2.5; that seems like the best compromise between size and unembedded text.
edits.comment: Fixes the comma splice and removes the unnecessary line break.

edits.title: Clarify smaller-ratio sentence
edits.find:
One thing I would note is chunks with smaller ratios are, IMO,
more likely to be noise. The logic goes as follows, sections that are 
heavily tokenized are likely to be rare words or formatted text.
edits.replacement: One thing I would note is that chunks with smaller ratios are, IMO, more likely to be noise. The logic goes as follows: sections that are heavily tokenized are likely to contain rare words or formatted text.
edits.comment: Adds the missing 'that' and fixes the comma splice before the explanation.

edits.title: Add colon before reasons
edits.find: for two reasons
edits.replacement: for two reasons:
edits.comment: A colon is expected before the numbered list.

edits.title: Fix RAG TREC wording
edits.find: before RAG TREC's submission date
edits.replacement: before the TREC RAG submission deadline
edits.comment: Use the event name consistently and make the deadline wording more natural.

edits.title: Clarify chunker improvements
edits.find:
The chunks and retrieval answers are now much better. I made 
changes to better preserve structure, run faster, and just in general be better written.
edits.replacement: The chunks and retrieval answers are now much better. I made changes to better preserve structure, run faster, and produce cleaner chunks.
edits.comment: 'Just in general be better written' is vague and awkward.

edits.title: Lowercase billion in range
edits.find: between 600-1.2 Billion chunks
edits.replacement: between 600 million and 1.2 billion chunks
edits.comment: Avoids an ambiguous range and normalizes capitalization.

edits.title: Clarify scaling option
edits.find: Scaling embedding
edits.replacement: Scaling embedding throughput
edits.comment: Makes the list item concrete.

edits.title: Fix data-loading phrasing
edits.find: I then would iterate over the items one at a time and chunk them from there.
edits.replacement: I would then iterate over the items one at a time and chunk them from there.
edits.comment: Use the standard auxiliary order 'would then'.

edits.title: Fix consistency intro punctuation
edits.find:
Given the number of machines running embeddings and two different endpoints 
(in my case GPU for bulk and CPU for single); it is important to be sure
that the embeddings generated are consistent.
edits.replacement: Given the number of machines running embeddings and two different endpoints (in my case, GPU for bulk and CPU for single), it is important to be sure that the generated embeddings are consistent.
edits.comment: The semicolon after the parenthetical is not appropriate.

edits.title: Remove duplicated return
edits.find: should return return the same embedding
edits.replacement: should return the same embedding
edits.comment: Removes the duplicated word.

edits.title: Fix occasional spelling
edits.find: ocassionally wild cards
edits.replacement: occasionally wildcards
edits.comment: Fixes spelling and uses 'wildcards' as one word.

edits.title: Fix embedding variance sentence
edits.find:
After some digging; embeddings seemed to vary 
from batch to batch to by a margin of 0.02-0.06 (this is rather large). Moreover, the same text embedded by CPU
edits.replacement: After some digging, embeddings seemed to vary from batch to batch by a margin of 0.02-0.06 (this is rather large). Moreover, the same text embedded by CPU
edits.comment: Fixes the semicolon and removes the stray 'to'.

edits.title: Fix similarity threshold wording
edits.find: Ideally we'd have a similarity of 0.99 or smaller.
edits.replacement: Ideally, we'd have a similarity of 0.99 or higher.
edits.comment: For similarity, higher is better; 'or smaller' contradicts the intended threshold.

edits.title: Fix compilation typo
edits.find: torch compilationm
edits.replacement: torch compilation
edits.comment: Spelling mistake.

edits.title: Complete GPU bullet
edits.find: 3. Intra-service (GPUs): I disabled overlapping schedule, radix caching, chunkfill, and fixed memory fraction. The GPU
edits.replacement: 3. Intra-service (GPUs): I disabled overlapping scheduling, radix caching, and chunked prefill, then fixed the memory fraction.
edits.comment: The original bullet ends with an incomplete sentence.

edits.title: Fix FAISS index wording
edits.find:
In other words an index can be made up of other indices which each add properties. Whether it be the distance used, quantization, use of IDs, use 
of disk instead of RAM, etc..
edits.replacement: In other words, an index can be made up of other indices, each of which adds properties such as the distance used, quantization, explicit IDs, or disk-backed storage.
edits.comment: Fixes a fragment and the double period after 'etc'.

edits.title: Fix flat index phrase
edits.find: The easiest type of index to use in FAISS is a FLAT, in memory index.
edits.replacement: The easiest type of index to use in FAISS is a flat, in-memory index.
edits.comment: Removes the unnecessary comma and hyphenates the compound modifier.

edits.title: Fix onset wording
edits.find: That pushed me from the onset towards a disk-backed IVF-style setup.
edits.replacement: That pushed me from the outset toward a disk-backed IVF-style setup.
edits.comment: 'From the outset' is the idiomatic phrase, and this removes the extra leading space.

edits.title: Fix training sample wording
edits.find:
Too many clusters requires
a large training set, which needs to all be stored in RAM.
edits.replacement: Too many clusters require a large training set, which all needs to be stored in RAM.
edits.comment: Fixes subject-verb agreement and word order.

edits.title: Remove double space and split long sentence
edits.find: The utility code should help you estimate the index size.  I now would estimate the target number of vectors, choose the IVF cluster count, sample enough embeddings to train that layout, and validate query latency before committing to the full run.
edits.replacement: The utility code should help you estimate the index size. I would now estimate the target number of vectors, choose the IVF cluster count, sample enough embeddings to train that layout, and validate query latency before committing to the full run.
edits.comment: Removes the double space and improves the adverb placement.

edits.title: Hyphenate trade-off
edits.find: be worth the trade off.
edits.replacement: be worth the trade-off.
edits.comment: Use the hyphenated noun form consistently.

edits.title: Fix CPU machine wording
edits.find: C3 8 core standard came clutch in here.
edits.replacement: A C3 8-core standard instance worked well here.
edits.comment: Replaces slang and hyphenates the compound modifier.

edits.title: Fix GPU recommendation
edits.find:
you may want to look 
at still using GPUs
edits.replacement: you may still want to look at using GPUs
edits.comment: Fixes the awkward word order.

edits.title: Clarify memory recommendation
edits.find: I would recommend high-memory machines (64 GB+, ideally 256).
edits.replacement: I would recommend high-memory machines (64 GB+, ideally 256 GB).
edits.comment: Adds the missing unit for 256.

edits.title: Fix serving phrasing
edits.find: Serving. I did it on the same machine as indexing, but really out of simplicity.
edits.replacement: Serving. I did it on the same machine as indexing, but really for simplicity.
edits.comment: Use 'for simplicity' rather than 'out of simplicity'.

edits.title: Fix ClimbMix casing
edits.find: all of climbmix indexed
edits.replacement: all of ClimbMix indexed
edits.comment: Use the dataset capitalization established earlier.

edits.title: Fix consumer-speed sentence
edits.find: Increasing number of consumers didn't increase speed, it stayed roughly the same or got worse
edits.replacement: Increasing the number of consumers didn't increase speed; it stayed roughly the same or got worse
edits.comment: Adds the missing article and fixes the comma splice.

edits.title: Replace HPs abbreviation
edits.find: Specifically finding best HPs
edits.replacement: Specifically, finding the best hyperparameters
edits.comment: Avoids an unexplained abbreviation and adds the missing article.

edits.title: Fix etc punctuation
edits.find: 100M docs, etc..
edits.replacement: 100M docs, etc.
edits.comment: Use one period after 'etc'.

edits.title: Complete response-time bullet
edits.find: 3. Evaluate the time required for responses (this would have helped
edits.replacement: 3. Evaluate the time required for responses.
edits.comment: The original bullet has an unfinished parenthetical.

edits.title: Fix affects/effects
edits.find: how scale effects the results
edits.replacement: how scale affects the results
edits.comment: Use the verb 'affects'.

edits.title: Remove conclusion indentation
edits.find: If I were doing this again, I would estimate index size and cluster layout earlier
edits.replacement: If I were doing this again, I would estimate index size and cluster layout earlier
edits.comment: Removes an unintended leading space at the start of the paragraph.
